label: text
text: DISPUTE BETWEEN CHINA AND SOVIET.

label: text
text: HOSTILITIES NOT LIKELY.

label: text
text: (Reutor's Service.)

label: text
text: Tokyo, Jun. 21.

label: text
text: The Diet re-opened this morning, after the New Year recess. Speeches were made by Viscount Kato, the Premier, and Baron Shidehara, K.E.E., the Foreign Minister.

label: text
text: Following their speeches this morning in the Upper House, Baron Sakatani grew attention to the growing gravity of the Sino-Russian situation and enquired about the "government's attitude." In reply, Baron Shideharstated that the matter was regarded purely as a Sino-Russian problem and unlikely to culminate in hostilities, though the Government was watching possible developments vigilantly test future action might be required.

label: text
text: Most of the morning papers offer no comment on the Sino-Russian friction, though the "Hochi" voices the opinion that the trouble is due to Chan Tsolin's desire to re-establish, his damaged prestige by stirring up Chinese national settlement in his favour.

label: text
text: The "Fleochii" forecasts in Chinese success, as the Soviet action is fettered by fear of damaging relation with Japan.

label: text
text:
According to an “Asahi” despatch from Duiren, Chang Tso-lin ordered the arrest of M. Ivanov. President of the Chinese Eastern Railway, and the Mukden authorities to resume the railway service by force if necessary.
A despatch to the “Asahi” from Harbin reports that the gravity is increasing and the Chinese troops are preparing to concentrate in Harbin in greater numbers.

label: text
text: According to Press reports, M. Kopp, the Soviet Ambassador to Japan, when interviewed, declared that "the Russian Government is prepared to back up its demands by force; if necessary meeting troops with troops."

label: text
text: In spite of all this, the vernacular papers generally indicate that the Japanese Government and people are maintaining a calm attitude.

label: text
text: KARAKHAN'S VERSION

label: text
text: HOLDS CHINA RESPONSIBLE.

label: text
text: M. Karakhan on Tuesday forwarded a Note to the Wai-chia-pus saying, inter alia, that Chinese soldiers on Saturday forcibly occupied the cars in the mail train which was in readiness to depart for Harbin. When the railwaymen demanded that they leave the train the soldiers forcibly seized the engine, took off the keys of the switches, stopped r.d.lway manouvring, and prevented the passage of a loaded freight train from Kuang Cheng-tze to Chang Chun.

label: text
text: As regards passenger traffic the violent actions of the Chinese soldiers were still more abominable. On Sunday the Chinese Military Headquarters arbitrarily and forcibly despatched the mail train to go to Harbin without awaiting at stations for the receipt of permits, and in spite of closed semaphores which, according to the railway regulations, constitutes a crime. Consequently, the switches were destroyed at many stations. Only through the exceptional measures being taken by the railwaymen this train failed, being wrecked with the consequent loss of lives.

label: text
text: MILITARY ENCOURAGEMENT

label: text
text: The outrages continue, the military leaders virtually encouraging them and evidently anxious to paralyse railway work in all sections. Furthermore on Sunday and Monday the Harbin Police were indifferent even encouraging, while a mob of upward a hundred committed social violence toward the railway agents

label: paragraph_title
text: RABIES POSITION.

label: text
text: LOCAL OUTBREAK NEARING ITS END.

label: text
text: NO FURTHER REPORTS.

label: text
text: No fresh occurrence of rabies has been reported to the Sanitary Department during the last few days.

label: text
text: The last case was that of a dog taken from Wyndham Street, which had been bitten by a pointer at Praya East. Both these have been destroyed, as reported.

label: text
text: Two dogs which played with the one in Wyndham Street are still under observation at Kennedy Town. In the brief interval it has not been possible to say whether they are infected. Subsequent inquiries indicate that all possible sources of spreading have been explored without success.

label: text
text: It is taken that this last outbreak is now in hand, the "tail end" stage having been reached.

label: text
text: end" stage having been reached. Recourse has not been deemed necessary to either the general muzzling order. (which was so effective in Britain), the vaccination of dogs, at $5 each, rendering them immune for a year (as is largely practised in Japan), or the putting out of poison baits at night.

label: text
text: Recently a large batch of prize dogs arrived here from Australia which is a “free country” as regards rabies, so that no fear is entertained in regard to them.

label: text
text: The lecture on February 1st at the Helena May Institute will be “The Story of Heligoland before and after the War”—not “Heavier-than-Air-Craft” as advertised. It is hoped that this lecture will be given at a later date.

label: text
text: M. Karakhan then protests energetically against the violation of the agreements between China and the U.S.S.R. He requests the Foreign Office to instruct the local authorities to put an end to the outrages, restore order, and inform him what measures have been taken.

label: text
text: M. Karakhan also points out that the U.S.S.R., having full regard for the sovereignty of China, renounced the protection of the railway on the presumption and hope that the Chinese would appreciate such a move and treat with particular consideration the interests of the railway entrusted to them. He regrets that the military leaders do not understand their duties, and requests the Foreign Office to enlighten them.

label: text
text: M. Karakhan says that he is likewise constrained to declare that, if the military leaders, whose duty is to protect the railway, are willing or unable to do so, he is ready to discuss with the Foreign Office the measures which are indispensable. He invites its attention to the seriousness of the situation and the necessity for taking extraordinary measures, and the grave consequences which may arise if the situation is allowed to continue, adding: "My Government will hold China responsible for all damage inflicted through the actions of the Chinese authorities as well as from outrages by the military."

text: “BELGENLAND” TOURISTS PROGRAMME

label: text
text: "Morning without programme, ricshas provided; afternoon also free for individual action." This being to-day's arrangements for two of the four groups of the "Belgenland" passengers, the local shops were again inundated and good business was done.

label: text
text: One group of nearly a hundred left for Macao this morning for a tour of the principal places of interest, visits to the fantaine-gambling houses, the grotto and garden of camoes, the facade of San Paulo, the Praia Grande etc. being included in the itinerary. They are due back at 6 p.m.

label: text
text: The remaining group spent an hour on the Peak this morning and joined the other "free agents" at the Hongkong Hotel for tiffin Tea at Repulse Bay will conclude an enjoyable morning and afternoon's outing for them.

label: text
text: To-morrow, Sunday and Monday, this programme will be reversed and at 5 p.m. on the latter day the "Belgenland" will sail.

label: text
text: Ship's Bereavement.

label: text
text: We regret to report that one of the “Belgenland” tourists, Mrs. Edward R. Bradley, wife of the prominent race horse owner of Lexington, Kentucky, died on board the boat early last Saturday morning at Shanghai of heart failure. Mrs. Bradley had not been able to leave her cabin since the ship left Yokohama.

label: text
text: When the ship left Yokohama, Mrs. Bradley became ill and although her condition was not regarded as serious, she did not leave the ship when the "Belgenland" anchored at Woosung, but remained in her cabin and told her friends that she did not feel able to go ashore. About midnight on Friday night her condition grew suddenly worse and despite the efforts of the ship's doctor, death came a short while after. The cause of death is given as heart failure.

label: text
text: An official inquiry was held aboard the “Belgeuland” prior to the body of Mrs. Bradley being taken to Shanghai on a special tender. Arrangements are being made for sending the body back to America. It is improbable that an inquiry will be held by the United States Court authorities in Shanghai since a physician was present.

label: text
text: SHOP ASSISTANT AND A CHEQUE

label: text
text: A Chinese shop assistant was brought before the Central Magistracy this morning on a charge arising from his failure to account for a sum of $1,950, a cheque for which amount was handed to him by his master to be cashed at the bank.

label: text
text: Defendant's explanation was that he gave the cheque to a friend to have it cashed. This man, he alleged, sent the money through a third party who had abscodded.

label: text
text: Detective: Sergeant McEwen obtained an adjournment to enable him to make inquiries.

Salary Inspector H F Strange, who caught one of the offenders at Clarence Terrace, produced a bundle of complaints from local holders and informed the Madate at the unlicensed hawkers were doing a roaring trade by a house to house staff within market limits.

label: text
text: MOTOR BOAT ABANDONED.

label: text
text: How ten men were saved on the high seas by a P. & O. steamer is briefly reported by Captain J. B. Browning, R.D., R.N.R., master of the "Khyber," on arrival here from Shanghai.

label: text
text: The ship left Yokohama, bound South, on January 12. At 4 p.m. on January 15, the crew of ten were taken off from the Japanese fishing motor boat "Iyo Maru," which was abandoned with two anchors down.

label: text
text: The position is given as Lat. 31.55 N., Long. 128.24 E.

label: text
text: RAID ON A GAMBLING DEPOT.

label: text
text: SIX MEN UNDER ARREST

label: text
text: At a raid carried out by Detective Sub-Inspector F. W. Shaftain, a quantity of Macao lottery tickets were seized in a house alleged to be a distributing centre.

label: text
text: Six Chinese arrested during the raid were brought before the Central Magistrate this morning and were severally charged with keeping a common, gaming house, printing announcement, and selling tickets.

label: text
text: The case was adjourned.

FINED.

label: text
text:
A Chinese passenger on the s.s.
"Amakusa Maru" pleaded guilty at the Kowloon Magistracy this morning to a charge of unlawful possession of an automatic pistol, two guns and 378 rounds of ammunition.

label: text
text: A fine of $500, or six months' imprisonment, was imposed.

label: text
text: OWNERSHIP OF LANDS AND MINERALS.

label: text
text: (Rent's American Service.)

label: text
text:
Mexico City, Jan. 21.
The new law regulating foreign ownership of lands, water, and minerals has been gazetted and comes into force today.

label: text
text: The latest development in the Mexican oil lands dispute is contained in an announcement by Mr. Guy Stevens, Director of the Association of Producers of Petroleum in Mexico, that the applications for injunctions recently filed by American oil companies against the new Petroleum Law have been refused by the First Supernumerary Court of Mexico.

label: text
text:
Mexico City, Jan. 21.
The British Minister, Mr. Esmond Ovey, visited the American Ambassador, Mr. Sheffield. It is believed that they discussed the respective British and American attitudes regarding the new Allen Land and Petroleum laws. It is understood that these attitudes are in perfect accord.

label: text
text: SOLDIERS LANDED NEAR HOIHOW

label: text
text: LOCAL GENERAL RESISTS.

label: text
text: (From Our Own Correspondent.)

label: text
text: Hohow, Jan. 18.

label: text
text: Several hundred troops despatched by the Canton Government landed last night at Foutai about 15 miles east of Hoihow, on the island of Hainan (separated from Kwangtung province proper by the Hainan Straits).

label: text
text:
General Tang Bunin (Tang Pun-yan), the pro-Chan commander who has vacated the mainland and whose forces now hold the island, sent several regiments, by motor cars, to fight the invaders.
There is the Golden River between Foutai and Hoihow so that the anti-Canton troops have a natural line of defence.

label: text
text: Shops in. Hoihow have closed their doors and are pursuing a waiting policy.

label: text
text: DELEGATES: REJECT BOARD'S AWARD.

label: text
text: CRITICAL CONFERENCE

label: text
text: (Reufer's Service.)

label: text
text: Trouble has again arisen in the railway world.

label: text
text: At to-day's conference of the branch delegates of the National Union of Railwaymen rejected the award of the National Wages Board which, after considering the Companies' claims for a reduction in wages and the men's counterclaims for increases, issued a report on December 9 practically maintaining the status quo. It is noteworthy that the men's leaders, Mr. J. H. Thomas (former

label: text
text: Though to-day's conference is generally regarded as the most critical since the last big strike, it is gathered that the decision merely reflects the movement for the re-opening of the negotiations, the delegates being not anxious to commit the Union to strike action.

label: text
text: The decision creates a delicate situation as the award is due to come into operation on February 1. The conference will again meet to-morrow to consider the next move.

label: text
text: Though it is believed that no decision for strike action will be taken until the Unions' Executive have met, the Companies have endeavoured to re-open the negotiations or secure a postponement of the application of the award.
